The Story of King Gandhamitra

I bow to Lord Jitendra, who is adorned with infinite virtues and brings welfare to the world, and I write the story of King Gandhamitra, who lost his life by becoming enslaved to the sense of smell.

King Vijaysen and Queen Vijayvati of Ayodhya had two sons. Their names were Jaysen and Gandhamitra. Of these, Gandhamitra was deeply lustful. Like a bee that flits from flower to flower, he was always absorbed in smelling various kinds of flowers.

One day, for some reason, their father Vijaysen became detached from the world. He gave the kingdom to his elder son Jaysen, made Gandhamitra the crown prince, and took initiation from the monk Sagarsen. Truly, good people are naturally inclined toward dharma.

Gandhamitra, the younger brother, did not like the position of crown prince, for his ambition was to be king. So, driven by greed for the throne, he conspired against his elder brother. He bribed many high officials with wealth, and through false advice, he misled many of the people. Gandhamitra succeeded in his plot. Seizing the opportunity, he drove his elder brother Jaysen from the throne and made himself king. Fools, caught in greed, will even try to take the life of their own brother.

Jaysen, deprived of his kingdom, was deeply grieved by his brother's injustice. He now devoted himself to finding a way to take revenge. Consumed by vengeance, he forgot his duty. He waited eagerly for the day when he could kill Gandhamitra and satisfy his heart.

Gandhamitra was lustful, and every day he would take his wives to the Sarayu River and play and frolic with them in the water. Jaysen considered this the perfect opportunity for revenge. One day, he had various beautiful and attractive fruits poisoned and floated them down the river. The flowers drifted past Gandhamitra, and as soon as he saw them, he lunged to grab them. He took some flowers in his hand and began to smell them. The poison took effect very quickly, and before long, he was dead.

After death, Gandhamitra went to hell due to his extreme craving for the objects of the sense of smell. And truly, Jaysen too, having committed the sin of murder, suffered greatly. He was eventually killed in a battle and fell into a lower birth.

This story teaches that attachment to any sense object — whether sight, sound, smell, taste, or touch — is a trap that leads to destruction. Gandhamitra's obsession with fragrant flowers led directly to his death. And Jaysen's obsession with revenge led to his own downfall. The wise should cultivate detachment from all sense pleasures and practise self-restraint, for these are the keys to liberation.
